claim: `ReportIfLocatedInCompilation` drops every diagnostic whose location is not in source, including `Location.None`. That covers source-declared types, not just metadata ones. The new `GetPropertyIdentifierLocation` uses `as PropertyDeclarationSyntax`, so for a positional record property (declared by a ParameterSyntax) it returns null. As a result, `BothStringAndIntKeyAreNull` for an in-source positional record property such as `[property: Key((string)null)]` is now silently discarded instead of reported. Before, it threw `InvalidCastException`. The acceptance criteria ask for no crash and for in-assembly types to keep working; they do not ask for errors on source types to disappear.

claim: The new reportDiagnostic wrapper drops every diagnostic whose Location is not IsInSource. Diagnostics that were previously reported with Location.None, for example when a null location is passed, are now silently suppressed. A user type whose diagnostic lacks a source location, such as one using GetLocation helpers that return null, no longer gets that diagnostic. This is a behaviour change for same-assembly types, which are meant to "keep working as before".

claim: ReportIfLocatedInCompilation wraps every analyzer diagnostic and silently drops any whose location is not in a syntax tree of the compilation. Diagnostics with Location.None are also dropped, so any existing diagnostic reported without a location is now suppressed (e.g. MemberNeedsKey, which previously could carry a null location). This could hide legitimate reports in the same assembly, and L10 warns that analyzer reporting changes risk wrong reports.
